title: audit-contrivance-scrap-notes-liv-2026
content:
Purpose: quick, messy personal notebook for mapping evidence -> control claims while prepping for SOC2 dry run. Not polished; capture who-to-ping, rough queries, risks that are fuzzy, and reminders for follow-ups.

High-level goals:
- Get minimal replicable evidence bundles for these controls: CC6.1 (change mgmt), CC7.1 (access mgmt), CC9.3 (logging/monitoring), CC8.2 (key mgmt).
- Make a concise checklist that an auditor can consume without 20 cross-references.
- Identify gaps we can fix before the formal readout.

Immediate open questions (to resolve with Samir/Evelyn):
- Which service accounts have long-lived keys in project-redwood-prod? quick list from GCP IAM (approx query below).
- Backup verification cadence for customer-configs: who runs the monthly restore test? (Ops runbook link?)
- Is there a single canonical runbook for "incident: leaked api key"? I thought there was one in SRE but can't find the latest version.

Evidence pointers (short hand):
- User provisioning (access reviews): ok, use OKTA report (last full review 2025-11) + Slack channel #onboard-offboard for attestation threads. Need export: OKTA CSV => archivist bucket: s3://redwood-sec-evidence/okta/2026-01-review.csv
- MFA enforcement: Admin console screenshot + policy id. Also fetch device_enrollment logs for last 90 days.
- KMS key rotation: KMS audit log snippet showing rotateKey event for kms/key-ring/infra-key on 2025-12-02. Grab Cloud Audit logs (bigquery).
- Config backups: snapshot list from backups-prod (gcs://backups/prod-configs/2026-01-05) + restore job id: restore-2026-01-20-rc1. Need evidence of verification run (stdout file).
- Deployment approvals/change control: PR -> CI -> canary deployment. Evidence set: GitHub PR #4451, codeowner approval + CircleCI build logs + rollout history from deploy-service (rolloutId=roll-667).

Quick ad-hoc queries / commands to run (notes to self):
- GCP IAM: "gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --project=redwood-prod --filter='createTime<2025-01-01'" then cross-check with active keys.
- BigQuery (logging):
    SELECT protoPayload.methodName, resource.labels.project_id, timestamp
    FROM `redwood-prod.audit_logs.cloudaudit_googleapis_com_activity_*`
    WHERE protoPayload.methodName LIKE '%cryptoKeyVersion%'
    ORDER BY timestamp DESC
    LIMIT 100;
- S3 list for evidence: "aws s3 ls s3://redwood-sec-evidence/okta/ --recursive --human-readable"

Control mapping snippets (raw, needs tidy):
- CC7.1 (Access provisioning): evidence = okta-offboard.csv (last 90d), access-review-email-thread (archived), policy doc (confluence:access-policies-v2). Owner: HR+IT.
- CC6.1 (Change mgmt): evidence = PR workflow (github PR + approvals), deployment audit (deploy-service logs), change request ticket (JIRA:CHG-1207). Owner: Eng-release.
- CC9.3 (System monitoring): evidence = Datadog alert config snapshot + pager duty incidents list for last 12 months + logging retention policy. Owner: SRE.
- CC8.2 (Cryptography / Key mgmt): evidence = KMS rotation events (cloud audit logs) + KMS policies + HSM usage note (for private deployments). Owner: Infra-security.

Risks I keep bumping into (prioritization suggestions):
1) Orphaned service-account keys: high probability, medium impact. Quick win: run scan, revoke keys older than 18 months, require rotation process.
2) Weak traceability for config restore testing: medium probability, high impact if we can't produce a verifiable restore. Need to schedule a live restore and capture logs.
3) Missing signed acceptance for emergency access: auditors look for explicit sign-off. Work with product manager to capture retrospective approvals.

Concrete next actions (owner / ETA):
- Samir: run IAM key-age scan, upload CSV to s3://redwood-sec-evidence/iam-scans/ (ETA 2026-03-07).
- Me (Aria): pull GitHub PR / deployment evidence for two representative change windows (2025-11, 2026-01), collate into one zip for auditor. ETA 2026-03-08.
- Evelyn: confirm backup restore job stdout exists and attach to backup evidence folder. ETA 2026-03-06.
- Ping SRE (channel @sre-oncall): ask for Datadog alert snapshots and PD incident exports for last 12 months. (I'll draft message).

Stuff to include in the "auditor-friendly bundle":
- One-page index.csv that maps control -> artifact name -> path -> brief description.
- PDFs/screenshots for policies (access, change, key management).
- Raw exports (okta csv, audit logs subset, PR list).
- A short narrative for each control (1–2 paragraphs) explaining the normal workflow + where evidence came from.

Draft message for Slack (to copy/paste):
> @sre-oncall hi team — quick favor. We're assembling artifacts for a SOC2 dry-run. Can someone export a snapshot of Datadog alerts (JSON) and PD incidents (CSV) for the period 2025-03-01..2026-02-28 and drop in s3://redwood-sec-evidence/monitoring/ ? If you can also point me at the canonical runbook for "key compromise" that'd help. Tag me if there's access permissions.

Random notes & heuristics (personal):
- Keep auditor bundles minimal: they hate hunting across buckets. Put a README at top-level in each folder.
- Timestamp everything in evidence file names (YYYYMMDD).
- When in doubt, include both summary screenshot + raw export.
- Avoid redacting logs unless necessary; prefer filtered exports with a README explaining filters.

Later follow-ups (backlog):
- Formalize access review cadence with HR (monthly/quarterly?).
- Add explicit acceptance checkbox to emergency access playbook.
- Automate an evidence packaging job that zips evidence for a control on-demand (stretch goal).

Links I keep referencing:
- Confluence:security/readiness-guide (we should copy the index into README)
- GitHub PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4451 (change mgmt example)
- JIRA: SEC-312 (key rotation follow-up)

End of messy notes. Will tidy into a 1-pager and index.csv once we have the raw exports.
